pr_body:
## Breaking Change:
Previously UniFi POE control switches had attributes showing network usage for receiving and transmitting data of that entity. This has been replaced with separate sensors, a pair per network client; one for received data and one for transmitted data. Default configuration is to keep this disabled so if you want to use this either enable select entities in the entity registry or go to your UniFi Integration options and enable it for all clients (see [HASS 0.98 blog post](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2019/08/28/release-98/#config-entry-options) for guidance).
<!-- What is breaking and why we have to break it. Remove this section only if it was NOT a breaking change. -->

## Description:
Adds sensors that will show RX/TX bandwidth usage per client. 

Haven't looked at potential extra relevant attributes to add to these sensors.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #25846

**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
0.97


**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
0.96.x

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
Hass.io

**Component/platform:**
Unifi

**Description of problem:**
The old Unifi integration creates various sensors for things like bandwidth.  That is, I could do the following:
```yaml
     monitored_conditions:
       - last_seen
       - rx_bytes
       - rx_bytes-r
       - tx_bytes
       - tx_bytes-r
```
and I would get a sensor for these for each tracked entity. 

Now those sensors are gone.  Please either bring back the sensors or add `rx_bytes`, `rx_bytes-r`, `tx_bytes`, and `tx_bytes-r` as attributes.

**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml

```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```

```

**Additional information:**
comments:
Hi!

We can't keep them as part of the default attributes of client trackers. See this issue for details: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues/25782

We can't allow configuration of extra attributes due to this architectural decision: https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0003-monitor-condition-and-data-selectors.md

Feel free to suggest another solution that can make fit within these limits

I'm not familiar with the Unifi API, so I presume based on your comment that you have to make separate API calls to get things like `rx_bytes` and thus violate the architectural decision.

If so, what's wrong with letting people use `monitored_conditions:` to specify the stuff that needs a separate API call?  It can't be "because we don't want to send the user to `configuration.yaml` because that's already needed for everything other than entering server/user/pass. 

I think the issue here is that the 'new' Unifi integration is a downgrade in functionality and it, IMO, was pre-mature to move everyone over when all previous functionality wasn't in the new integration - or at least preserve the option to configure the 'old' way until such time as the new one is brought to parity.

No it is all in one API call. The reason why it can't be enabled by default is the amount of extra data that it generates when doing extra logging.

This change regarding monitored conditions would have happened sooner or later when moving integrations in line with architectural decisions.

What Im trying to do now is to move forward and find suitable solutions on making as many people happy as possible. Feel free to chime in on how to solve this.
Ive had a talk with balloob about ways to solve this. He will add gui support for config entry options, after that I can implement enabling this.
Any news / issue we can follow, to get an idea when this will be fixed?
Its on my list, can't say when it will be done yet
I've started implementing support for client bandwidth sensors now. Do you really need all 4 rx_bytes, rx_bytes-r, tx_bytes, and tx_bytes-r?
Well, I personally do not need the -r variants...

review_comments: We should be able to drop these attributes now from the Unifi PoE switch entities?
Absolutely. Some cleanup, possible attributes and tests left
So what is happening here? Are we going to first show 1 screen, then another screen ?
Since it's just one option, can't we put them in 1 screen ?
Im planning to add other sensors later on, so I'd rather group them together. This is also why I think enabling descriptions would be a good improvement, describing the theme of the options.
